features.name: Chat
features.note: Checked live on the owner's account in W1.

features.name: Switching tool inside a chat
features.note: Opens a new chat beside the old one after one confirm. The text goes to the other vendor.

features.name: Several accounts, limit switch
features.note: Automatic moves between tools stay off.

features.name: Brain, recall, task log
features.note: Runs the same hooks. In a chat the write gate on marketing tokens and agent files works only after `dreamcontext install --tool codex` and trusting the folder and its hooks. The live check is the owner's.

features.name: Automations
features.note: No home board, no task steps. Sandboxed with no network, so a job that needs the web stays on Claude. Runs only after `dreamcontext install --tool codex` and trusting the folder and its hooks in Codex, which is what keeps writes off `_dream_context/marketing/.env` and agent files. Reading a `.env` is open, as on Claude.

features.name: AI Team agents
features.note: Same limits as automations. Changing the tool asks for approval again.

features.name: Super Agent
features.note: The lead stays on Claude: its verbs are off the brain MCP on purpose.

features.name: Super Agent's delegated child
features.note: `super delegate --tool codex`. stdio MCP servers only, and the same write gate as automations.

features.name: Terminal
features.note: `codex` on the chat's account, always workspace-write.

features.name: Sleep
features.note: `sleep auto-run --tool codex`. One turn with no sub-agents. No live run recorded yet.

features.name: Antigravity chat
features.note: Experimental. Checked live on one account: sign-in, memory, approval cards, resume, the Bypass write gate. Eco and account moves are proved against a fake agent only. It has no OS sandbox, so the agent always asks: Auto and Accept Edits show a card, and under Bypass the bridge answers except for marketing tokens and agent files, so a Bypass agent can write outside the project. Automations, Super Agent, AI Team, Terminal and Sleep stay off it. OpenCode was dropped by the owner. Core skills go in each account's profile and the brain MCP server rides the session, with no project step: both proved against a fake agent only. Context rides in the user's message, because ACP has no untrusted channel.
